- [USER] Is it possible to create a file with the extension .css for css code?
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Yes, you can create a file with the extension ".css" to store your CSS code.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To do this, simply create a new file in a text editor (such as Notepad or Sublime Text), add your CSS code to it, and save the file with a name of your choice, followed by the ".css" extension.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] For example, you could create a file called "style.css" and save it in the same directory as your HTML and JavaScript files.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Then, in your HTML file, you would link to the CSS file by adding the following code to the head section: `<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="style.css">`.
